key_insight: A deep learning competing-risk model using only pre-treatment oncology data can accurately identify women with breast cancer at higher 1-year cardiovascular event risk before therapy starts.
clinical_relevance: This could help oncology teams triage patients for earlier cardio-oncology referral using information already available at the first visit.
method: Registry-based cohort of 17,051 women with stage I-III breast cancer or DCIS in Stockholm-Gotland (2008-2019)
Model used demographics, cancer features, planned treatment, comorbidities, medications, and healthcare utilization available before treatment
Performance assessed with 3-fold cross-validation, time-dependent concordance, and Fine-Gray models for interpretability
evidence_signal: Validation showed strong and stable performance, with median c-index 0.84 for 1-year MACE prediction and 0.90 for the competing-risk outcome.
watch_item: External validation and prospective testing are still needed before routine deployment, especially because performance may vary across health systems and treatment workflows.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Pretreatment Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Women with Breast Cancer
